llm_notes:
1. **Fix the title/H1 to match query intent, not brand-only branding.** Add comparison-led landing pages with titles like “AeroGarden Bounty vs Harvest: Which Is Better for Small Apartments?” and “AeroGarden vs Click & Grow: Best Indoor Garden for Beginners?” so the page directly matches your GSC demand instead of a generic Sill-style brand title. Keep one clear H1 per page, and use the same keyword pair in the intro so the page is obviously about the comparison, not just a product roundup.

2. **Add a top-of-page comparison table above the fold.** Ship a simple 5–7 row table for each target query with columns like Price, footprint, setup time, pod compatibility, app/Wi‑Fi, best for, and maintenance. For example, on “AeroGarden Farm vs Farm Plus,” include footprint, grow sites, light height, Wi‑Fi/app support, and apartment fit; on “Click & Grow vs AeroGarden,” include seed refill model, automation, and noise/maintenance. Make the table visible before the first long paragraph so users get the answer fast.

3. **Add a FAQ block that resolves purchase objections.** Mirror what peer sites are already doing by adding 5–7 concise FAQs under each comparison page: “Which is better for apartments?”, “Which system is quieter?”, “Which has lower ongoing pod costs?”, “Which is easier for beginners?”, “Do I need Wi‑Fi?”, and “Which grows faster?” Keep answers to 2–3 sentences and include one direct recommendation per answer. This gives you more long-tail capture and a better chance to own snippet-style answers.
